newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Tung counted among China elite - report.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Tung counted among China elite - report.

text.p: Hong Kong's chief executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa has been officially included in the elite ranks of China's highest leaders, a Hong Kong newspaper said on Monday.

The HongKong Standard said Tung, who will succeed British Governor Chris Patten when Britain pulls out on July 1, would be ranked equivalent to a "state leader", the label attached to the 70 or so figures in China's leadership pantheon.
The newspaper, whose report was unsourced, gave no details about Tung's rank or title in relation to other senior officials, such as Premier Li Peng.
Hong Kong has been rife with speculation that Tung would be ranked in Beijing as a minister or state councillor and might get a seat in the Chinese Communist Party's ruling Politburo.
Tung's spokesman was not immediately available to comment on the report in the independent English-language daily. Beijing has made no announcement on Tung's position in the hierarchy.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.
Tung, a former shipping tycoon, was chosen as post-colonial leader by a 400 member China-controlled committee last December.
